title: Explain the harvesting of animal products

lessons.title: Animal products and food safety principles
lessons.html:
What are animal products?

Harvesting animal products means collecting what animals produce in a way that keeps the product safe, clean and valuable while protecting the animal's welfare. Main products on South African farms include:

  • Milk from dairy cows and goats.
  • Eggs from layer hens.
  • Fibre: wool, mohair and cashmere.
  • Meat and hides from cattle, sheep, goats, pigs and poultry.
  • Honey and beeswax.

Food safety principles

Most products go into the human food chain, so hygiene and residue control are critical.

  • Withdrawal periods: after an animal is treated with a stock remedy or veterinary medicine, its milk, eggs or meat may not be used until the withdrawal period on the label or prescribed by the vet has passed. Treated animals must be clearly marked and recorded.
  • Hygiene: clean hands, clean protective clothing, clean equipment and clean animals.
  • Cold chain: perishable products such as milk, eggs and meat must be cooled quickly and kept cool.
  • Healthy workers: workers with diarrhoea, infected wounds or contagious illness should not handle food products and must report it.
  • Traceability: records should allow every batch to be traced back to the animals and treatments involved.

Legislation

The Meat Safety Act 40 of 2000 requires that animals for sale as meat are slaughtered at registered abattoirs under meat inspection. Animal welfare during harvesting is protected by the Animals Protection Act 71 of 1962. Follow your farm's and buyer's quality standards as well.

lessons.title: Harvesting milk and eggs
lessons.html:
Milking

Good milking routine protects udder health and milk quality.

  1. Bring cows in calmly. Stress reduces milk let-down.
  2. Wear clean clothes and gloves. Wash hands.
  3. Fore-strip the first few streams from each teat into a strip cup to check for clots, blood or watery milk, which are signs of mastitis.
  4. Pre-dip or clean and dry teats with individual paper towels.
  5. Attach the cluster within about a minute of preparation, as the let-down reflex fades.
  6. Avoid over-milking. Remove the cluster when flow drops.
  7. Post-dip teats with an approved teat dip.
  8. Cool milk promptly in the bulk tank and keep it at the temperature your milk buyer requires.

Milk from cows with mastitis or under treatment must be kept separate and discarded as directed until the withdrawal period is over. Mark treated cows clearly, for example with leg bands, and milk them last. Clean the machine, tank and parlour after each milking using the correct detergent and sanitiser.

Collecting eggs

  • Collect eggs several times a day so they stay clean and cool and are not broken or eaten.
  • Keep nest boxes clean with fresh nesting material.
  • Handle eggs gently, pointed end down in trays.
  • Separate cracked, dirty and abnormal eggs.
  • Store eggs in a cool, clean area away from strong smells and chemicals.
  • Do not sell eggs from hens under treatment until the withdrawal period is over.

lessons.title: Fibre, slaughter animals and honey
lessons.html:
Fibre

Wool and mohair are harvested by shearing, usually once or twice a year depending on species and system. To protect the value of the clip, shear only dry animals, keep the shed free of plastic and rubbish, skirt and class fleeces, and pack one line per approved wool pack. Protect freshly shorn animals from cold weather.

Animals for meat

  • Select animals that meet the market's mass and condition requirements.
  • Check treatment records. Animals within a withdrawal period may not be sent to slaughter.
  • Handle and transport animals with low stress. Stress and bruising lower meat quality and cause carcass trimming losses, and dark cutting beef can result from stress before slaughter.
  • Send animals with correct identification and documents to a registered abattoir, as required by the Meat Safety Act 40 of 2000.
  • Hides and skins are valuable by-products; avoid brand damage, wire cuts and tick damage through good management.

Honey

  • Harvest only capped honey frames, leaving enough honey for the colony.
  • Wear a bee suit, veil and gloves and use a smoker.
  • Extract in a clean, bee-proof room with food-grade equipment.
  • Do not harvest honey while hives are being treated with anything not approved for that use.

Records and quality

For every product, keep records of dates, quantities, the animals or groups involved, treatments and withdrawal periods, and quality results from the buyer, such as milk somatic cell counts, egg grades, wool test results or carcass grades. Use these to find and fix problems.

Key points

  • Animal products enter the food chain, so hygiene and residue control come first.
  • Respect withdrawal periods on the label or from the vet for milk, eggs, meat and honey.
  • Follow a consistent milking routine and cool milk promptly.
  • Collect eggs often and handle them gently.
  • Send slaughter animals with low stress to a registered abattoir.
  • Keep records for traceability and quality improvement.

quiz.question: A cow was treated with an antibiotic. When may her milk go into the bulk tank?

options.text: Only after the withdrawal period on the label or from the vet has passed

quiz.question: Why is fore-stripping done before milking?

options.text: To check for clots, blood or watery milk that show mastitis

quiz.question: Which law requires animals sold as meat to be slaughtered at registered abattoirs?

options.text: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993

quiz.question: Why should eggs be collected several times a day?

options.text: To make hens lay bigger eggs
So eggs stay clean and cool and are not broken or eaten

quiz.question: What effect does stress before slaughter have on meat?

options.text: It can lower meat quality and cause dark cutting beef
It makes the meat more tender

quiz.question: Only capped honey frames should be harvested, leaving enough honey for the colony.
A worker with diarrhoea may continue handling milk as long as they wear gloves.
Which steps belong in a good milking routine? (select all that apply)

options.text: Post-dip teats with an approved teat dip
Cool milk promptly in the bulk tank
Use one shared cloth for all cows
Milk treated cows last and keep their milk separate
Leave the cluster on long after milk flow stops
